Subject: Private cluster: escape-hatch and version shelving for June patch

Team,

We need to finalize the "escape-hatch" and version-shelving approach for Oakridge's private deployment maintenance next week. Goal is to pin, stage, and provide an explicit fallback that can be executed remotely by their Ops team if the rolling upgrade regresses.

Key asks from my side:
- A brief, ordered playbook (3–5 steps) we can hand to Oakridge for emergency unpin/eject.
- A version-shelving matrix that maps active runtime -> compatible rollback artifact + required KV/cache reset steps.
- Maintenance window options that minimize patient-facing impact (they prefer early Sat/Sun).

I attached a first draft of the escape-hatch procedures and an initial shelving matrix (see attachments). Please review and flag non-starters by EOD Monday.

Attachments: escape-hatch-procedures.md (MD), version-shelving-matrix.csv (CSV)

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Thanks Priya — quick technical notes after a first pass: 

1) Rollback artifact: for the current service image (v2.7.x) the safe fallback is the v2.6.8 build with the compatibility patch we validated last quarter. That artifact is already signed and stored in our private registry under tags: oakridge/v2.6.8-signed.

2) KV cache considerations: rolling back requires a KV cache reset on the inference nodes (we call it "KV tombstone"). We can either drain and warm caches from a pinned snapshot (preferred) or perform a force-evict. The force-evict is faster but increases cold-start token latency for ~5 minutes.

3) DB migrations: none in this patch, good. If we see schema-level changes we must abort.

I added line items in the attached CSV where the operator must run: `kv_reset --mode=snapshot --snapshot-id=...` and where to expect a 3–8 min window of elevated token latency.

Attachment referenced: version-shelving-matrix.csv (updated)

-Karthik
Senior Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the questions, Lena — answers and final decisions below.

1) KV snapshot restore ownership: Redwood will own the restore action when the customer requests it. We will provide two modes: 
   - Assisted: Redwood on-call executes `kv_restore --snapshot=<id>` via an authenticated runbook session (we provide temporary RBAC token).
   - Operator-led: Oakridge runs the documented commands; we provide step-by-step commands in the escape-hatch doc for their on-call.

   For this engagement we propose Assisted mode for the first two rollouts (Oakridge approves) to reduce risk. If Oakridge prefers Operator-led, we will do a quick run-through with Jamie ahead of the window.

2) Visibility for force-evict: Grafana will show a token-latency spike with an alert we can set to `p95 > 350ms` for 5 minutes. We will create a dashboard panel called "KV-evict latency" and add it to the Oakridge shared view. If the p95 threshold breaches for more than 5m during canary, we will abort to the shelving artifact.

3) Escape-hatch condensed playbook (customer-facing, 3 steps):
   a) Pause rolling update and mark canary nodes unschedulable (we provide the command).
   b) Execute `kv_restore --snapshot=<stable-snap-id>` or run the assisted restore (Redwood).
   c) Re-pin nodes to v2.6.8-signed and validate health. If all green, de-schedule maintenance.

Action items: 
- Karthik: add the `kv_restore` commands and Grafana panel instructions to the escape-hatch doc (by EOD Tuesday).
- Monica: schedule the Sun 03:00–06:00 window and invite Oakridge on-call if they want the operator-led option.
- Dev/Soojin: produce a short test script we can run in the canary to validate KV freshness and inference correctness (small prompt set).

I attached the final escape-hatch and the shelving matrix (updated). Please confirm and I'll send the formal change notice to Oakridge.

Attachments: escape-hatch-procedures.md (final), version-shelving-matrix.csv (final), maintenance-window-proposal.ics
